question: Why does unconditionally setting the session access tracking attribute in dictionary access methods impact signed cookie string conversion performance during frequent read operations?
answer: Because every read (e.g., `session["key"]`, `session.get()`) sets `accessed = True`, Flask treats the session as "touched," and with the default `SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST=True`, `save_session` then runs `serializer.dumps(dict(session))` — the expensive dict→JSON→compress→base64→HMAC signed-cookie-string conversion — on every response, even though no data actually changed. So pure read operations repeatedly pay the full serialization/signing cost instead of skipping it when the session is unmodified.
